sections.label: B
sections.title: Complete the sentences.
sections.note: Use one word or phrase from the box. One item is not needed.

questions.prompt: 1. The bear sometimes runs and ___ across the ice to reach the other side of the river.
questions.explanation: Glides means moves smoothly across a surface.

questions.prompt: 2. There are ___ in North America, Russia, China, and Japan. They have lots of trees with leaves that change colors in the spring and autumn.
questions.explanation: Temperate forests have seasonal weather and many trees whose leaves change color.

questions.prompt: 3. Polar bears hunt for fish and seals in the ___ where they live.
questions.explanation: The Arctic is the cold northern region where polar bears live.

questions.prompt: 4. A ___ is a plant that isn't easy to touch. It can hurt your finger if you're not careful.
questions.explanation: A cactus often has sharp spines, so it can hurt your finger.

sections.label: D
sections.title: Circle the correct answer.
sections.note: Use since for a starting point and for for a length of time.

questions.prompt: 1. We have been friends ___ 2006.
questions.explanation: 2006 is the starting point, so use since.

questions.prompt: 2. My mother has studied biomes ___ ten years.
questions.explanation: Ten years is a duration, so use for.

questions.prompt: 3. My father has been a teacher ___ a long time.
questions.explanation: A long time is a duration, so use for.

questions.prompt: 4. I have gone to this school ___ September.
questions.explanation: September identifies the starting point, so use since.

sections.label: E
sections.title: Complete the sentences for each set of pictures. Use the present perfect.
sections.note: Use since with the starting time and for with the duration shown under each picture.

questions.prompt: 1a. She / study butterflies / 2003
questions.explanation: Use has studied with since because 2003 is the starting point.

questions.prompt: 1b. He / study butterflies / five years
answers: He has studied butterflies for five years
questions.explanation: Use has studied with for because five years is a duration.

questions.prompt: 2a. She / talk on the phone / 2:00
answers: She has talked on the phone since 2:00
She has talked on the phone since 2 o'clock
questions.explanation: Use has talked with since because 2:00 is the starting time.

questions.prompt: 2b. He / talk on the phone / two hours
answers: He has talked on the phone for two hours
questions.explanation: Use has talked with for because two hours is a duration.

sections.label: F
sections.title: Combine the sentences.
sections.note: Write one present-perfect sentence using the word in parentheses.

questions.prompt: 1. We study biomes. We started two weeks ago. (for)
answers: We have studied biomes for two weeks
questions.explanation: The action began two weeks ago and continues now, so use have studied + for two weeks.

questions.prompt: 2. I am on the soccer team. I joined the team in May. (since)
answers: I have been on the soccer team since May
questions.explanation: May is the starting point, so use have been + since May.

questions.prompt: 3. He lives on Main Street. He moved there in 1995. (since)
answers: He has lived on Main Street since 1995
questions.explanation: 1995 is the starting point, so use has lived + since 1995.

questions.prompt: 4. My bedroom is blue. I painted it three months ago. (for)
answers: My bedroom has been blue for three months
questions.explanation: Three months is a duration, so use has been + for three months.

sections.label: J
sections.title: Look and write sentences. Use the present perfect or simple past.
sections.note: Use the time expression to decide which tense is needed.

questions.prompt: 1. She / snorkel / yesterday
questions.explanation: Yesterday is a finished past time, so use the simple past: snorkeled (US) or snorkelled (UK).

questions.prompt: 2. We / already / visit / that beach
answers: We have already visited that beach
We already have visited that beach
questions.explanation: No finished past time is given. Use the present perfect, placing already between have and visited.

questions.prompt: 3. He / hike / in the mountains / last week
answers: He hiked in the mountains last week
questions.explanation: Last week is a finished past time, so use the simple past hiked. The subject in the prompt is He.

questions.prompt: 4. I / not see / sea turtles / yet
answers: I have not seen sea turtles yet
I haven't seen sea turtles yet
questions.explanation: Use the negative present perfect have not seen, with yet at the end.

sections.label: K
sections.title: Complete the sentences.
sections.note: Use one word from the box. One item is not needed.

questions.prompt: 1. I have ___ lots of seahorses in the marine park.
questions.explanation: After have, use the past participle seen.

questions.prompt: 2. You studied hard, but did you ___ everything you needed to?
questions.explanation: After did, use the base form learn.

questions.prompt: 3. I ___ a turtle on the beach yesterday.
questions.explanation: Yesterday requires the simple past saw.

questions.prompt: 4. Have you ___ about sharks in school?
questions.explanation: After have, use the past participle learned; learnt is also correct in British English.

questions.prompt: 5. Did you ___ Sarah to your party?
questions.explanation: After did, use the base form invite.

sections.label: L
sections.title: Write the words in the correct order to make questions. Then listen and write the answers.
sections.note: Make each present-perfect question first, then play the audio and write the short answer.

questions.prompt: 1. studied / Have / seahorses / they

parts.label: Question
parts.explanation: Use Have + they + past participle studied.

parts.label: Listening answer
parts.explanation: The recording gives the positive short answer: Yes, they have.

questions.prompt: 2. ever / he / manta ray / a / Has / seen

parts.label: Question
answers: Has he ever seen a manta ray
parts.explanation: Use Has + he + ever + past participle seen.

parts.label: Listening answer
parts.explanation: The recording gives the negative short answer: No, he hasn't.
